mostWorthwhile.text: Using the spindle was most worthwhile: the time-strip connects chromosome attachment and separation to two nuclei, while making clear that the cytoplasm remains connected.

leastWorthwhile.text: The grown-cell picture repeats the DNA-copying explanation already shown earlier, making that passage feel repetitive.

surprise.text: The spindle result is explicitly a preview of assembly during mitosis rather than an already assembled structure with chromosomes attached; the time-strip clarified the timing.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, although several were the only offered combination. The spindle preview introduces tubulin and motor arrows without much explanation of how the motors move fibres.

continue.text: I would probably continue: the distinction between nuclear and cytoplasmic division was useful, and the dotted paths toward different cell types suggest an interesting next connection. The largely forced sequence makes the gameplay less compelling, though.
